title: Definitions of the Passions of the Rational Soul
english: Chapters 33 (Definitions of the passions of the rational soul) of Evagrius the Monk, in order. 1. Idiosyncrasy is a disposition of the rational soul, by which it mistakenly perceives both God and the contemplation of things happening. 2. Retrogression is an evil of the rational soul, by which it becomes resistant toward virtue and the knowledge of God. 3. Agitation is a heat and a movement of the thymos, the rational part of the soul, unsettling it. 4. Blindness is an ignorance of the intellect, not applying itself upon practical virtues and the contemplation of things happening. 5. Paralysis is a sluggishness of the rational soul toward practical virtues. 6. Sloth is a listlessness of the rational soul, by which it is accustomed to cast away the words of spiritual teaching. 7. Deposition is an incapacity of the rational soul, by which it is accustomed to cast away the virtues that work toward the formation of Christ. 8. Leprosy is an unbelief of the rational soul, by which, feeling its way, it is not made certain of the words.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
